title: cockpit-synthetic-monitoring-spec
universal_lens: The synthetic monitoring cockpit formalizes a discrete-time Markovian state machine over a categorical partition of system health. It unifies temporal observation windows, hierarchical failure propagation, and operator-induced control perturbations into a single topological manifold of observables.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the 96-point sparkline to a conformal prediction sequence, treating yellow warnings as epistemic uncertainty bounds. Auto-filed issues act as posterior updates to the latent reliability distribution of the underlying production environment.
gse_mapping: GSE models the dashboard as a situational awareness lattice. Manual re-runs and runner pauses represent active control inputs that force non-stationary state transitions, requiring real-time recalibration of the expected system trajectory.

primitives.name: 24-Hour History Sparkline Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 24-hour history sparkline Per check, a horizontal sparkline of last 96 results (24h × 4 per hour).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N = 96 (dimensionless count), Δt = 15 min (time interval), T = 24 h (observation window)
primitives.assumptions: Stationary sampling frequency; discrete binary or ternary state outcomes per interval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if the 15-minute heartbeat desynchronizes or drops packets, corrupting the temporal density of the sparkline.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's rolling window feature extraction for athlete fatigue metrics, mapping discrete event streams to continuous reliability surfaces.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of state transitions across the 96-point window.

primitives.name: Auto-Filed Issue Queue Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Auto-filed issues When a check fails and the runner auto-files to `docs/ops/issue-queue.md`, the entry appears here as a linked card.
primitives.assumptions: Deterministic mapping from a terminal failure state to a persistent documentation artifact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the file system is read-only or if concurrent failures cause race conditions in the markdown queue.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's automated injury report generation, translating raw sensor anomalies into actionable tactical adjustments.
layer2.telemetry: Latency between S_fail occurrence and I_queue creation.

primitives.name: Manual Control & Pause Override
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pausing requires a decision-log entry explaining why + expected resume timestamp.
primitives.assumptions: Operator intervention is an exogenous shock to the autonomous monitoring loop.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System enters an undefined blind spot if u(t)=0 exceeds τ_resume without manual resumption.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE coach overrides during live play-calling, injecting human priors to halt algorithmic execution based on contextual meta-knowledge.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of manual overrides vs. automated alerts.

reasoning_traces.think:
The cockpit specification defines a rigorous discrete dynamical system where the state space Ω is partitioned into six categorical domains (e.g., Bot/AI surface health). The core observable is the 96-point sparkline, representing a sliding window W_t = {x_{t-95}, ..., x_t} of ternary states (pass, warn, fail). This forms a finite-state Markov chain where transition probabilities P(x_{t+1}|x_t) dictate the system's reliability. The 'auto-filed issue' acts as a boundary condition: when x_t enters the 'fail' basin of attraction, a deterministic map Φ projects this state into a persistent external ledger (the issue queue). This creates a dual-layer topology: the ephemeral runtime state and the permanent historical record. Manual interventions, such as pausing the runner or forcing out-of-cycle checks, introduce non-autonomous control vectors u(t). These vectors temporarily decouple the system from its natural 15-minute periodicity, effectively freezing the Markov chain or forcing a synchronous reset. The requirement for a decision-log upon pausing ensures that every control vector is accompanied by a metadata payload (justification, expected resume time), preserving the causal graph of the system's evolution. The breakdown regime occurs when the monitoring system itself loses connectivity (the red indicator), collapsing the entire observational manifold into a single point of total ignorance.

The cockpit serves as the interface where the Operator attempts to infer the hidden state of the Environment by interpreting the compressed sparkline signals and deciding whether to apply manual control overrides.
